text:
— I am not making a scene; I am only telling you that I cannot go on without seeing you, without speaking to you now and then. In short, listen, Loretta: I have fallen in love with you, foolishly in love, because all this serves only to make you laugh... Yet you will understand that one does not give up in a single day the thing dearest to one.

— I have never laughed at you, Rafa, — she said gently.

— Yes, laughed, laughed, and you want to do nothing but laugh!... But it does not matter. I am only telling you this, Loretta: do not think of taking away from me that very little which you have granted me until now, because in that case I do not know what might happen.

That timid man had found a tone so full of energy that Loretta was astonished by it.

— Come now, Rafa, calm yourself, — she said. — Do not take things this way, and do not look at me like that, because you almost frighten me. I should like you to reason instead, to think of one thing, of one thing only: What if my brother were to find out?...

— He will not find out.

— Oh, that is easily said! You do not know him; he is capable of... I know what he is capable of! In short, I should be a ruined girl, and let that suffice for you.

Rafa calmed down a little in the face of such arguments.

— Very well, we shall increase our precautions; I shall do whatever you wish.

— In this world, my dear, everything comes to be known, and when we suppose ourselves well hidden, a thousand eyes are watching us.

— But in short, this danger existed before as well, and yet...

— Precisely, precisely; it is something that cannot go on any longer. I have been imprudent, very imprudent with you, but I cannot go any further.

— Loretta, — he said softly, in a persuasive voice, — think that I love thee, think that thou art in my thoughts all day long, that thou art so deeply in my soul that I cannot give thee up... Do not be so cruel, I beg thee!

He took hold of her arm, and she did not try to draw it away.

— Be quiet, Rafa... — she murmured, — be quiet!

But he went on:

— I have left everything behind, solely to enjoy these few moments thou givest me. Thou seest, I am not demanding, I shall insist no more; for now I am content to see thee, to speak to thee now and then... If one day thou wert to break off so abruptly the sweetness of the love I bear thee, it would have been better never to allow me to draw near thee. Now it is too late.

— But no, Rafa, thou... you do not understand!

— I understand perfectly; I am a matter of indifference to thee, I amused thee for a little while, and now thou hast had enough; thou art afraid, and darest risk nothing for me.

— You do not understand, I tell you. If I had no family, if I did not have so many appearances to preserve, if, in short, I were free, alone... then, perhaps... But as things are, I repeat, woe, woe if my brother were to have the slightest suspicion of this!

— We shall make sure he knows nothing.

— No, Rafa. And then there is another danger...

— What danger?

— Oh God! There is another danger, I tell you; do not insist.

— Come, out with it, tell me! Be honest for once!

They were walking; she stopped and assumed a mischievous air:

— Why dost thou address me as “thou,” for example? Thou knowest very well that I do not want thee to.

— That does not matter; go on: what is the danger?...

— In short, you say that I laugh, that I laugh... It is easy to say! Yet it might be that, when all is said and done, I too was afraid that I might cease to laugh...

— How I love thee, Loretta! — he exclaimed ingenuously, encircling her waist with one arm.

— Keep still... keep still, come now! — And she continued: — Naturally, I too am made neither of wax nor of tow... One day or another, what do I know? finding ourselves alone, for example, with the things you are always saying to me... or by chance, or by mistake, or for any other reason at all, I might perhaps lose... In short, it takes no time at all to commit a foolish act!

She twirled her parasol again, thrust it deep into a hedge, and added:

— And then?...

Rafa tried to answer, but she gave him no time:

— Of course, you men are quick about it: good day, good evening, and that is the last one sees of you! We girls pay for both. The thoughtlessness, the intoxication of a moment, may cost us who knows what price, and you say that one laughs? Naturally one laughs, one laughs... as long as one can...

— But I am an honorable man, Loretta! — he proclaimed resoundingly.

— Very well. And because you are an honorable man, I ought to give myself to you? That is not a good reason, do you think? But I, dearest Rafa, have my whole life to live, and there are, I repeat, certain reasons of my own which forbid me the luxury of doing what perhaps I too would enjoy. I am certainly not a street girl, nor do I have, like some other woman, a coat of arms and several millions to assure me of impunity. If I found myself in either of those two situations, well then, yes, I might perhaps be the sort to say to a man—to you, for example: “My dear Rafa, I like thee; do with me what thou wilt.” But in my case this would mean offering you my entire life, gambling my whole future, material and moral, on the recklessness of a moment... And that is a little too much, do you not think?

Having delivered this fine speech to him, she involuntarily thought of Arrigo, regretting that he could not hear her. She felt like saying these two words to herself; indeed, she said them inwardly: “How clever you are!”

Rafa took some time to extricate himself from his difficulty; during that interval they both passed once more in front of the old man who was reading the newspaper one syllable at a time, and through the greenery, along another path, they saw the infantry soldier returning with his ruddy maidservant.

— Loretta, — he said at the end of that silence, — I have already spoken to thee once with great clarity; but thou wilt not even hear certain things discussed.

— I know very well what you are alluding to!... — she said sarcastically. — Since we have spoken of it once, we may speak of it again. And I prefer clear situations and plain words. You offered me money... a great deal of money!...

— Not like that, Loretta... — he exclaimed, blushing.

— Just like that, just like that! What is the use of circumlocutions? That is the naked truth.

She paused, and he did not dare interrupt her.

— Now listen, Rafa. I do not know what opinion you have of me; indeed, I do not care. Everything may lead you to believe that I am capable even of selling myself... and that does not offend me, because once again I admit that the fault was mine. You see that I am speaking openly, as I have not done before. Nevertheless, if you believe that, you are mistaken. I need nothing: from my family I receive everything I require, and I could receive much more if I were willing to submit to certain family disciplines that are contrary to my character. We are not extremely rich, yet you can see that my brother, for example, leads an enviable life. If I wished to marry tomorrow, I could choose, and choose well, as my sister did, for I have a sister too. But none of this pleases me. I have already told you that I am a girl unlike the others. Precisely because of my singular ideas, I have already come into conflict with my family; I have laid claim to a kind of independence, and I would have done even more if I were not afraid of my brother in particular.
